hypotheses.statement: For a known static physical force direction, the reported world-frame force has its primary response aligned with that physical direction under one globally determined sign convention.
Reversing the physical force direction produces a reliable sign reversal in the corresponding reported component.
For the same world-referenced physical force direction at different tool orientations, the reported world-frame direction remains world-consistent rather than rotating with the tool.
Zero-load baseline wrench can be quantified and pose dependence can be identified without assuming its controller/sensor origin.
Host query timestamps are sufficient for steady-state static averaging but do not validate controller-source timing or dynamic synchronization.
